mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one NBER-defined recession window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fails to activate during any NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline of at least 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >= 1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger activates but no recession is present.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 0.5% in the housing starts index (HOUST) and a year-over-year increase of at least 3% in personal savings (implied by RSAFS decline) signals a rebalancing toward consumption, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises >= 0.5% AND RSAFS falls by >= 3% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger activates outside a post-recession recovery window.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and inflation, which raises discount rates and ultimately produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase of at least 0.8% in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 0.2% for three months signals an expansion with slack labor, boosting output without wage inflation, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises >= 0.8% AND UNRATE < 0.2% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger activates outside an early-cycle expansion.
